title: Cryoprotection, flash-cooling and loading crystals into pucks
summary: Quickly dip the crystal in cryoprotectant (or oil), plunge it into liquid nitrogen in under a second, and transfer the pin into a labelled puck under LN2 for storage in a dewar. Compiled from a practical cryocrystallography review.

steps.text: Decide on cryoprotection: grow in a cryoprotectant if possible (glycerol, ethylene glycol, PEG 400, sucrose at 25-50%), or briefly soak or oil-coat the crystal.
Dip the looped crystal for 1-15 seconds in cryoprotectant, minimising carry-over; for oil, coat and dab off excess.
Plunge the crystal into fresh liquid nitrogen in under one second with one continuous motion.
Transfer the pin into a puck with pre-chilled tongs within seconds, keeping everything below the LN2 surface or in cold gas.
Record position and unique ID for each pin (steel 1 mm pins suit robotic handling).
Store loaded pucks in canes or canisters submerged in a dewar until shipping.

safety: Liquid nitrogen: wear eye protection and cryogenic gloves; asphyxiation risk in small rooms.
Keep dewars covered to limit ice; avoid skin contact with cold tools.

source.publisher: Acta Crystallographica Section F (IUCr, via PMC)

notes: Review article, so numbers are general guidance rather than a single lab's recipe. Per-step durations are literature ranges.
